purpose: Per-fact evidence for pack.json (CMP-029). pack.schema.json has no per-fact evidence field and caps notes at 500 characters, so sources live here. Labels: VERIFIED-OFFICIAL (official source read, per the cited repo doc), SECONDARY (treat as UNVERIFIED), UNVERIFIED, PLATFORM-DEFAULT (a platform choice, not a statutory claim). Access dates are those recorded in the cited repo doc; no source was re-read in this session. NOT legal advice.

facts.claim: The chart is the CMP-006 Saudi trading chart, referenced by path and version range, not copied. No component manifest exists for it yet, so componentId finance.coa_sa_trading names a component still to be registered. Adoption needs accountant review (Q-8).

sources.note: SOCPA endorsement of IFRS for SMEs, cited by CMP-006

facts.claim: VAT applies in KSA (15% from 2020-07-01). The rate and the seven treatments live in the CMP-006 file vat_treatments.json, referenced here; the pack holds no rate.

sources.note: cited by CMP-006 for the 15% rate

facts.claim: VAT returns are filed monthly or quarterly; which one applies is set per taxpayer by ZATCA.
Commercial rounding, half away from zero, so credit notes mirror invoices. A founder decision, not a ZATCA rule.
A KSA VAT registration number has 15 digits and starts and ends with 3. The rule was not re-read; the Blueprint contract today checks only 15 digits.

sources.note: XML standard cited by CMP-006; the VAT number rule in it was not read

facts.claim: A commercial registration number has 10 digits, as the Blueprint contract already assumes for KSA.

ZATCA e-invoicing Phase 1 (generation) has applied to all taxpayers since 2021-12-04; the pack uses the existing compliance.zatca_sa Phase 1 component. Phase 2 integration applies by wave and is a per-customer setting (country-matrix K3), not a pack default.
A tax invoice must carry its details in Arabic and may be bilingual. Printing English as well is a platform default (Arabic and English equal, principle 4), not a legal requirement.
Six-year retention is commonly cited; do not rely on it until the resolution is read.
KSA uses one time zone, the IANA zone Asia/Riyadh. The loader checks that the zone exists; no official source was read.
Commerce and tax run on the Gregorian calendar; Hijri (Umm al-Qura) is shown as a second date. No official Hijri requirement was found; ZATCA XML is believed to use Gregorian dates.
The weekend is Friday and Saturday; the work week runs Sunday to Thursday. Companies can override it.
facts.ref: docs/architecture/calendars-and-locale.md section Week, weekend and working time

facts.claim: 08:00 to 17:00 is a platform default that companies override. The statutory daily and weekly limits in the Labour Law were not read.
Shorter Ramadan hours (09:00 to 15:00, six hours) for Muslim workers, as the Labour Law is commonly reported to require. Not read.
Gregorian year from 1 January is a platform default; companies may choose another start or a Hijri year. Whether zakat needs a Hijri year is open (CMP-025).
facts.ref: docs/architecture/calendars-and-locale.md section Fiscal year and periods

facts.claim: Holidays come from the sa.holidays calendar, which CMP-024 builds; it does not exist yet. The pack holds no holiday dates.
Western digits, a dot for decimals, a comma for thousands and day/month/year dates are platform display defaults; the user can switch to Eastern Arabic digits.
The currency is the Saudi riyal (ISO 4217 SAR) with two decimals. ISO 4217 was not read.
Payroll, WPS (Mudad), GOSI and end-of-service are off: payroll is out of v1 scope and arrives with CMP-015 and CMP-016 (gate G3). The underlying rules are unread.
The tax invoice and simplified invoice use the locked ZATCA layouts of the ERP-007 print formats; the legal layout always wins over tenant branding.
